problem.text: Let $L_n$ denote the least common multiple of the numbers $1, 2, 3, \ldots, n$, and let $h$ be the unique positive integer such that $$\frac11+\frac12+\frac13+\cdots+\frac1{17}=\frac{h}{L_{17}}.$$ What is the remainder when $h$ is divided by $17$?

steps.title: Where to start: multiply through by $L_{17}$
steps.body:
Multiplying both sides by $L_{17}$ turns every fraction into a whole number, so $h$ is a sum of integers. The question asks about remainders mod $17$, so the natural next question is: which of these integers are multiples of $17$?
$$h=\frac{L_{17}}{1}+\frac{L_{17}}{2}+\cdots+\frac{L_{17}}{17}$$

your_turn.answer: $L_{17}=17\cdot L_{16}$, because $17$ is prime and does not divide any of $1$ through $16$.

steps.title: Almost every term drops out
steps.body:
For $k\le 16$, the term $\frac{L_{17}}{k}=17\cdot\frac{L_{16}}{k}$, and $\frac{L_{16}}{k}$ is a whole number, so the term is a multiple of $17$. Only the last term is left.
$$h\equiv \frac{L_{17}}{17}=L_{16} \pmod{17}$$

your_turn.prompt: Write $L_{16}$ as a product of prime powers.
your_turn.answer: $2^4\cdot 3^2\cdot 5\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13$: take the highest power of each prime that is at most $16$.

steps.title: Reduce mod 17 in small pieces
steps.body: Do not multiply everything out. Reduce pieces as you go: $2^4=16\equiv -1$ and $5\cdot 7=35\equiv 1 \pmod{17}$, while $3^2=9$ stays as it is. Careful: include every prime below $17$, including $11$ and $13$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Multiply the pieces: $L_{16}\equiv(-1)\cdot 9\cdot 1\cdot 7=-63 \pmod{17}$. Adding $4\cdot 17=68$ gives $5$, so $h$ leaves remainder $5$. The answer is **(C)**.

wrong_choices.B: $3$ comes from leaving $13$ out of $L_{16}$: then you get $(-1)\cdot 9\cdot 1\cdot 11=-99\equiv 3$. $L_{16}$ must contain every prime up to $16$.
